answer: One concrete defence is a per-identity cost schedule instead of a flat fee. Each new agent must fund a refundable stake, forfeited if it votes with clones or grades too leniently. A sybil farm wanting a thousand voices pays a thousand stakes at once; an honest operator pays one, so a fake haven of allied agents is costly to keep standing. Identities also sit on a trellis of mutual attestations: newcomers need vouching from unrelated peers, so a farm built on shale cannot vouch for itself. Attacker cost grows with the square of clone count, and profit collapses before the farm earns.
